newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Schmidhuber-no inflation danger in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Schmidhuber-no inflation danger in Germany.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Peter Schmidhuber said on Thursday there was little evidence of inflationary pressure in the German economy at the moment, despite a weaker mark and strong exports.
Schmidhuber said a combination of the current weakness of the mark against the dollar and the strength of the German export sector was not leading to imported inflation.
"Inflationary pressure has not increased and there is no reason to react with a change in interest rate policy," Schmidhuber said in an interview on n-tv television late on Thursday.
Schmidhuber said it was too early to discuss whether or not Germany would meet the three percent budget deficit criteria set out in the Maastricht Treaty.

"It is too early to discuss whether it will be 3.0 percent, 3.1 percent or 3.2 percent. We will be able to judge better in the third or fourth quarter of this year. There are too many components involved," Schmidhuber said.

There has been much debate of late whether or not Germany will meet the three percent of gross domestic product state deficit criteria in the Treaty, which sets targets for would- be members of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
EMU is due to begin on January 1 1999.
